newsitem.title: FRANCE: French ministry sees lower wheat yield - sources.
newsitem.headline: French ministry sees lower wheat yield - sources.

text.p: France's farm ministry expects the average yield for the 1997 soft wheat crop to decline to 6.8 tonnes per hectare from 7.27 tonnes last year, grain industry sources said on Monday.

The ministry sees barley yields falling to 5.8 tonnes per hectare from 6.19 tonnes and durum wheat yields to 3.7 tonnes from 4.65 tonnes last year. Rapeseed yields are set to decline to 2.97 tonnes from 3.33 tonnes. The ministry is expected to release its first estimate for the 1997 crop in coming days.

Based on the ministry's estimates of total spring and winter sowings of 4.901 million hectares, the new estimate puts the 1997 soft wheat crop at 33.3 million tonnes against a record 34.7 million for 1996.
The barley crop would, however, rise to 9.512 million tonnes from 9.463 million as a sharp 7.2 percent rise in total sowings to 1.640 million hectares would offset lower yields.

Using a sowings figure of 262,000 hectares for durum wheat, output would fall sharply to 969,400 tonnes from 1.254 million tonnes. Based on total sowings of 959,000 hectares, the rapeseed crop would drop to 2.848 million tonnes from 2.913 million.

The national grain office ONIC targets 1997 yields of 6.9 tonnes for soft wheat, 5.8 tonnes for barley and 3.6 tonnes for durum, industry sources said last week. Using sowings estimates released by ONIC on June 11, this would put the 1997 harvest at 34.2 million tonnes for soft wheat, 9.34 million tonnes for barley and 924,624 tonnes for durum.
